brief.headline: Tighten payment to 30 days to free up ₹2.25 L cash and test the market at ₹0.65–0.80/piece at higher volume.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹0.65–0.80/piece on our caps at higher committed volume or looser tolerance
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/piece (the lower end of the market range)
priceAsk.basis: Open market for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps shows ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc; the market verdict is MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec — so there is room to move down if we commit volume or relax a specification

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt

brief.financialLeverage: This supplier publishes no financials, so we cannot see their revenue, profit, debt, or how tight their cash is. Our ₹27.42 L spend is small in absolute terms, so we are unlikely to be a huge customer for them. Because we have no visibility into their health, the safest play is to line up a strong second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) before we push hard on price or terms — that way if they walk or stumble, we are covered. Without their numbers, our leverage comes from the market benchmark and from having a credible Plan B ready to quote.

evidence.point: Our annual spend with them is modest
We currently pay 45 days after receipt
Cutting 15 days (to 30-day terms) frees up cash for us
Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is a wide band
Typical market range clusters in the middle
Market verdict shows modest downward room at scale
evidence.figure: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health B (65/100) — a top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); strong, profitable — a robust alternate for bottles/closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: Pan-India manufacturer (medium confidence) — verify capability and MOQ before issuing RFQ

risks: No public financials: we cannot tell if they are healthy or struggling, so any aggressive push is a blind bet — qualify a second source first.
Small spend (₹27.42 L) gives us limited clout — they may not bend much on price unless we bundle volume or longer commitment.
Market bandwidth is wide (₹0.55–1.20/pc): without knowing what spec or volume drives the low end, our ask for ₹0.65–0.80 must come with a clear volume or tolerance trade-off.
Payment-term tightening saves us ₹2.25 L but may squeeze their cash if they are small or illiquid — watch for pushback or requests to offset it in price.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to 30-day payment to free up ₹2.25 L on our side, and at the same time explore whether a higher volume commitment or a spec adjustment gets us closer to the ₹0.65–0.80 market range we're seeing for similar caps.
